title.value: Efficient Planning under Partial Observability with Unnormalized Q Functions and Spectral Learning
title.justification: The title clearly encompasses the core contributions and focus of the paper.
title.quote: Efficient Planning under Partial Observability with Unnormalized Q Functions and Spectral Learning

analysis.description: This paper proposes a novel algorithm that integrates learning and planning in partially observable domains within reinforcement learning. The approach introduces an unnormalized Q function using spectral learning techniques which unify learning the environment dynamics and planning, making it more sample and time efficient compared to traditional methods relying on predictive state representations (PSRs). The empirical evaluation shows superior efficiency in partially observable grid world and S-PocMan environments.

type.justification: The paper focuses on empirical evaluations of the proposed algorithm through experiments on specific domains such as grid world and S-Pocman, indicating an empirical research type.
type.quote: We conduct experiments on partially observable grid world and S-PocMan environment [12] where we compare our approach with classical PSR based methods.

name.justification: The paper addresses problems and solutions related to planning and learning in environments modeled as POMDPs within Reinforcement Learning paradigms.
name.quote: Learning and planning in partially-observable domains is one of the most difficult problems in reinforcement learning.

name.justification: The paper discusses integrating reward information directly into learning, distinguishing it from traditional methods where reward estimation and environment learning are separate.
name.quote: instead of explicitly learning the dynamics of the environment, we learn a function that is proportional to the action value function, which we call unnormalized Q function (UQF). In doing so, we incorporate the reward information into the dynamics in a supervised learning fashion.

name.justification: The paper extensively deals with POMDPs as a research topic and often contrasts the proposed method with existing POMDP planning techniques.
name.quote: Partially observable Markov decision Processes (POMDPs) [29, 8] provide a formal framework for single-agent planning under a partially observable environment.

name.justification: PSRs are frequently mentioned as a baseline and comparison point for the proposed method throughout the paper.
name.quote: One common approach for modelling the dynamics of a POMDP is the so-called predictive state representations (PSRs).

is_contributed.justification: The paper uses PSRs as a baseline for comparison, indicating that it is an existing method, not a contribution of this paper.
is_contributed.quote: As an alternative to exact planning, the family of predictive state representations (PSRs) has attracted many interests.

is_executed.justification: While PSRs are discussed and used as a thematic backbone, there is no indication they are executed as part of a novel implementation within this study.
is_executed.quote: The PSRs parameters are learned independently from the reward information, resulting in a less efficient representation for planning.

is_compared.justification: The proposed method is empirically compared against PSRs, demonstrating its efficiency.
is_compared.quote: We conduct experiments on partially observable grid world and S-PocMan environment [12] where we compare our approach with classical PSR based methods.
